public_health_question.v: How prepared for disasters or emergencies are households in two metropolitan Tennessee counties, as assessed through CASPER training exercises?

ev.q: to 1) assess household-level preparedness in two major metropolitan areas in Tennessee, 2) evaluate the field team deployment process
Assessment of Household Preparedness Through Training Exercises
The CASPER two-stage cluster sampling design was used to obtain representative samples of approximately 210 households for interviews for each assessment.
At each household that participated, one adult representative was interviewed.

equity.level_reason: No social-position dimension is analyzed; results are given only by county, which is geography. Adulthood only defines the respondent.

level_alternative.reason: A limitation notes underrepresentation of households whose adults work outside the home, which could be read as a social-position limitation.

equity.equity_measurement: Only county-level (geographic) comparison; no demographic breakdown reported.

notes: County percentages are set side by side with no computed contrast or inference; the two counties asked different plan questions. CASPER weighting is not stated, so no weighting procedure is recorded. Design inferred as cross-sectional survey; the exercise's process-evaluation aim yields no quantities.
